full_judgment: 2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the petitioner alongwith others, as plaintiffs, instituted Title Suit No. 59 of 1990 in the court of Assistant Judge, Ulipur, Kurigram, against the opposite party Nos. 1-8, as defendants, for declaration that the Kabala deed No. 9989 dated 17-9-1988 was obtained by practicing fraud, null and void and liable to be cancelled, stating that the property under CS Khatian Nos. 339, 618 and 416 belonged to Zenat, Nurjahan Bibi, Atorjan Bibi and Nesmon Bibi. Zenat died leaving sons Sazor, Yeaz and Moyez and daughters, Mohiron, Kabjan, Ziron and Khonjon. Nurjahan, Atorjan, Nesmon and Ziron sold 0.94 sataks of land to the plaintiffs and their brother Nezabuddin. The plaintiffs sold 28 sataks of land to Aziron Nesa and Anower Hossain, rest of the land have been enjoying and possessing in ejmali. The plaintiffs instituted Other Suit No. 704 of 1994 for partition in respect of the suit land and other property against the defendants in suit, the suit was decreed on 1-8-1987. Against the decree of the trial court, the defendants preferred appeal before the District Judge and during pendency of the said appeal, the plaintiffs purchased 37 sataks of land from the defendants by a sale deed dated 17-9-1988. For the purpose of registration of the said deed, when they went to the Sub-Registry Office with the defendants the deed writer told the plaintiffs that in purchasing property, the purchasers also required to put their signatures on the deed. The plaintiffs on good faith believing the deed writer put their signatures and thumb impressions on some stamp papers and went to the Sub-Registry Office for obtaining registration of the purchase deed from the defendants. Thereafter, the defendants started pressure upon the plaintiffs to compromise the dispute knowing that they will not succeed in the appeal. When the plaintiffs refused to the proposal of the defendants they disclosed that the plaintiffs sold the property to them by a sale deed No. 9989 dated 17-9-1988. On hearing the said fact from the defendants, the plaintiffs have become highly astounded. The plaintiffs never sold any property and executed and registered any deed on acceptance of any consideration money from the defendants. The defendants are very cunning and shrewd men and they in connivance with deed-writer, identifier and the witnesses, taking advantage of illiteracy of the plaintiffs managed to obtain the signatures and thumb impressions of the plaintiffs, on the plea that the purchasers are required to sign the deed and created the sale deed without knowledge of the plaintiffs and without any consideration. The plaintiffs, after coming to know about the said fraudulent deed, obtained true copy of the same on 2-8-1989 from the concern registry office and finally came to know that the deed was obtained by them fraudulently showing the value of the same at Taka 200 only for 49 sataks of land which is unheard of and beyond imagination. Hence, the present suit for cancellation of the said deed.
